Not printed as a layer diagram on the card.</td><td>Blog [cite:3]</td><td></td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>OpenAI’s models page, fetched 2026-10-14, lists gpt-6-astra, gpt-6.1-sol, and gpt-6-luna at a 1.05 million-token context and a 128 thousand-token max output. It does not publish depth, width, head count, or a positional scheme. You can compare context windows. You cannot compare head counts, because one side did not publish them. Behemoth appears in the blog as a previewed teacher, not as a model-card file this room read as a shipped checkpoint. Do not quiz a teammate on Behemoth’s layer count. [cite:6] [cite:3]</p><h3>Where this sits next to retrieval and tools</h3><p>Attention inside the block reads the tokens that are already in the window. It does not open a database. If the refund policy is not in the prompt, no head will retrieve it. Packing a chunk into the window, which T3 teaches, gives attention something to mix. A tool result, which T4 teaches, is more tokens in that same window after the host executes. The host does not run inside a head. MCP revision 2025-11-25 keeps execution in the host. The changelog’s sampling-with-tools change asks the client to sample. It does not move the side effect into Q, K, or V. [cite:7]</p><p>Lost-in-the-middle, Liu et al., is a historical claim that models can use information at the start and end of a long context better than information in the middle. The paper is arXiv:2307.03172. It is not a measurement of Scout’s 10 million-token window and not a measurement of your contact-center prompt. Cite it as a reason to test position, not as a score you can paste onto a bot. [cite:8]</p><h3>Four prompts, the same head</h3><p>Keep the toy head fixed and change only the tokens you imagine in the window. The arithmetic does not become a vendor trace. It becomes a way to talk about four contact-center failures without blaming “attention” for all of them.</p><p>Prompt A is the policy paragraph at the start and the caller’s sentence at the end: “credits over fifty dollars need a human.” The query at the last position can put weight on “fifty” and on “human.” If the sample then says “I have applied a two hundred dollar credit,” the failure is not that the dot product was undefined. The failure is that a token was chosen which the policy paragraph does not authorize, and that a tool, if one ran, was allowed to commit. Attention could have mixed the word “fifty” into the last position and the sampler could still have picked “two hundred.” Mixing is not obedience. The fix is the tool cap from T4 and the faithfulness check from T5, not a larger d_k.</p><p>Prompt B moves the same policy sentence into the middle of a long transcript, with small talk on both sides. Liu et al. would tell you to suspect the middle. Your job is smaller: copy the sentence to the end, call the model again on a fixture, and see whether the abstention returns. If it returns, you have a position effect on this id, and you still do not have their tables. If it does not return, the model was not using the sentence even when it was adjacent to the query, and rearranging the prompt will not save you. Write down which of those two you observed. A story about “lost in the middle” without that swap is a citation wearing a costume. [cite:8]</p><p>Prompt C is a tool result that arrived after the caller barged in. The text in the window says the assistant already finished a sentence the caller never heard, because nobody truncated. Attention will mix that unheard sentence into the next query, because the mask only hides the future, not the past you failed to delete. The repair is T7’s truncate, not a new positional scheme. iRoPE does not know which audio reached the speaker. The blog’s temperature scaling of attention will not drop tokens you left in the prefix. [cite:3]</p><p>Prompt D is an empty window except the user text “what is the outage in Dallas?” No status page was packed. Every head, at every width the paper ever used, can only mix the words Dallas and outage with whatever the weights already store. The next token may be fluent. It is not a reading of a page you did not provide. This is the same boundary T1-R01 draws among weights, the window, and a tool. Attention is the mixer of the window. It is not a fourth place a fact can live.</p><p>Across the four prompts the head’s formula did not change. The mask did not change. What changed was the set of keys. When you are on call, ask “which keys were in the prefix?” before you ask “is attention broken?” The prefix is the prompt you built, the tool results the host appended, and the tokens the sampler already chose. The projections are the vendor’s, unless you are serving a checkpoint whose license you have read. For Llama 4 that license is the Community License. For an API model the projections are not yours to edit, and the card may not even list their shapes. [cite:9] [cite:6]</p><p>A useful review habit is to separate three sentences you are otherwise tempted to fuse. Sentence one: “the 2017 block has residual attention and a position-wise feed-forward network.” Sentence two: “Llama 4 Scout is a mixture-of-experts model with 16 experts and a 10 million context field on the card.” Sentence three: “this bot’s last answer contradicted paragraph 4.” Only sentence three is an incident. Sentence one explains a paper. Sentence two explains a card. Neither sentence selects a root cause for the credit. People who skip to a heatmap are trying to make sentence one do sentence three’s job. It cannot.</p><p>If you teach this room out loud, compute the toy once on a board and then refuse every follow-up that asks for Scout’s head count. The refusal is the lesson. The card spent its numbers on experts, active parameters, context, tokens, cutoff, GPU hours, and emissions. It did not spend them on h or d_model. An interviewer who wants eight heads wants the paper. Give them the paper, labeled historical, and then give them the card. Candidates who can only give one of those two will ship a diagram that matches neither system. [cite:1] [cite:2]</p><p>One more distinction belongs in the same breath as the experts. A mixture-of-experts model does not run every expert on every token. The card’s “17 billion activated” against “109 billion total” is the sentence that says so for Scout, and the same shape, with 128 experts and 400 billion total, is Maverick. The routing that picks experts is not drawn in the card and not drawn in this room. Do not invent a router diagram and attribute it to Meta. What you can say is that the active count is the compute the card claims per token, and the total count is the parameters that exist. Interviewers who add 17 and 109 have misread both numbers. Active is not a remainder. [cite:2]</p><p>Early fusion, the other phrase on that card, means the model is natively multimodal rather than a text model with a vision encoder bolted on in a way the card would have had to describe separately. The card says input can be multilingual text and image, and output is multilingual text and code. It says image understanding was tested with up to five images. It does not say a contact-center screenshot is in domain, and it does not publish a word-error rate for a phone call. Bring images into a lab only when the card’s input column includes them, and still evaluate the task you care about. A five-image test on the card is not a five-screenshot warranty for a desktop assist product. [cite:2]</p><p>Supported languages on the card are twelve: Arabic, English, French, German, Hindi, Indonesian, Italian, Portuguese, Spanish, Tagalog, Thai, and Vietnamese. The card also points at a broader pretraining mixture and at the No Language Left Behind work for a set on the order of two hundred languages. Those are different claims. A bot that must answer in a language outside the twelve should not be justified by the two-hundred figure alone. Say which list you are using. The same care applies to the emissions line: 1,999 tons CO2eq location-based, and zero market-based because the card states net-zero operations since 2020. Neither number is a latency budget. Both are part of reading a card all the way down, which is the habit this track is for. [cite:2]</p><h3>04Walk-through</h3><p>A caller says “you charged me twice.” The application has already decided, outside the model, that the allowed context is the last four turns plus one policy paragraph. This walk-through is the forward pass on that string. It is not the dial plan.</p><ol><li>Tokenize. The rendered prompt, including whatever template the provider owns, becomes integer ids. The lab’s tokenizer is a toy. Check the tokenizer docs for the model id you call. Merge rules differ by family, which is why the toy table is not the production one.</li><li>Embed and position. Each id becomes a vector. The 2017 paper adds a positional encoding because the network has no recurrence and no convolution. A Llama 4 checkpoint, per the blog, uses iRoPE instead of that sinusoid. An OpenAI chat id on the fetched models page does not name its scheme. [cite:1] [cite:3]</li><li>Masked attention. For the newest position, queries dot with keys of this position and earlier positions only. Scale, softmax, mix values. Several heads, then the output projection. The toy numbers above are the shape of this step at d_k = 2, not the shape inside Scout.</li><li>Residual and feed-forward. Add the attention output back, normalize as the paper’s block does, run the position-wise network, add and normalize again. Repeat for the stack depth the card actually states. If the card is silent, say silent.</li><li>Logits and sample. The last position’s vector becomes a score per vocabulary id. Temperature, if you set it, divides those logits. OpenAI’s chat-completions reference documents a temperature between 0 and 2 and says it generally recommends altering temperature or top_p, but not both. That page does not say that 0 is greedy argmax. Check the sampling section of the endpoint you call. Behavior at the bottom of the range varies by implementation, which is why this room will not teach that 0 means argmax. [cite:4]</li><li>Append and repeat. The chosen id is appended. Its key and value can be cached. The next position attends over a longer prefix. Stop on a finish condition or a length cap. max_completion_tokens on that OpenAI reference includes reasoning tokens. [cite:4]</li></ol><p>If step 3 is pictured as a heatmap on the words “charged” and “twice,” you still have not shown that the refund tool should run. The heatmap is a mixing weight. The tool decision is a later sample, and the host still has to allow it. T4 is the allow. This room is the mix.</p><h3>05Config path</h3><p>There is no switch labeled “attention” in a normal chat request. You configure the model id, the prompt, and the sampler. The projections were learned before you called. The path below is what you can rehearse without a provider console. Check the console for the account you use. Menu labels differ by product and by tenant, which is why a screenshot from another org is not a step.</p><ol><li>Read the model card for the id you will call. For Llama 4, that card is the Scout and Maverick file cited here. For the OpenAI ids in T1-R01, use the models page and accept that depth and width are absent. [cite:2] [cite:6]</li><li>Record context length and max output from that page, with the fetch date. Do not copy 512 or 8 heads into the record.</li><li>If you serve the weights, read the license beside them. Llama 4 is the Community License, effective 5 April 2025, not MIT. [cite:9]</li><li>Set sampler fields from the API reference you actually call. The chat-completions reference recommends altering temperature or top_p, but not both. It does not forbid sending both. [cite:4]</li><li>Leave attention-temperature scaling alone unless the runtime documents it. The Llama 4 blog describes it as part of iRoPE inference. It is not the request body’s temperature field. [cite:3]</li><li>Refuse any debug UI that claims a faithful explanation until that claim has a source. The mark on that claim stays until the source exists.</li></ol><h3>06Limits and numbers</h3><div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th>Limit</th><th>Value</th><th>Source</th><th>Stable enough to ship on</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Attention formula</td><td>softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k)) V</td><td>[cite:1]</td><td>Yes, as the 2017 definition.</td></tr><tr><td>Base model shape</td><td>N=6, d_model=512, h=8, d_ff=2048</td><td>[cite:1]</td><td>Yes, as history. A leaf ends in a citation or a TODO-verify.</p><h3>L0 · What does one attention head output?</h3><p>A vector that is a weighted sum of value vectors. The weights are a softmax of scaled query–key dots. [cite:1]</p><h3>L1 · Why divide by the square root of d_k?</h3><p>The paper’s reason is to keep the dots from growing with dimension and saturating softmax. In the toy, d_k is 2, so you divide by about 1.414 before the exponentials. [cite:1]</p><h3>L1 · What does the causal mask change in the toy?</h3><p>If the second key is in the future, its score is negative infinity and its weight is zero. The output is the first value alone. [cite:1]</p><h3>L2 · What is multi-head attention in the paper?</h3><p>h independent attention computations, concatenated, then projected. The base model uses h = 8 and d_model = 512, so d_k = 64. Historical. [cite:1]</p><h3>L2 · What does the residual do?</h3><p>It adds the sublayer output back to the sublayer input before layer normalization, so the block updates the stream instead of replacing it. [cite:1]</p><h3>L2 · What does the feed-forward sublayer mix?</h3><p>Features at a single position. It does not mix across positions. Attention already did that. The base inner width is 2048. [cite:1]</p><h3>L3 · Is a chat model the 2017 encoder–decoder?</h3><p>Not by default. The paper has both stacks and three uses of attention. A chat model is often decoder-only. Llama 4’s card says auto-regressive mixture-of-experts and does not draw the 2017 diagram. [cite:2]</p><h3>L3 · What is iRoPE, and where did you read it?</h3><p>The Llama 4 blog: RoPE on most layers, interleaved layers without positional embeddings, and inference-time temperature scaling of attention. The model card’s context field is a different sentence from the blog’s 256K training length. [cite:3]</p><h3>L3 · Scout versus Maverick, in one breath?</h3><p>Both activate 17 billion parameters. Scout is 109 billion total, 16 experts, 10 million context on the card, about 40 trillion tokens. Maverick is 400 billion total, 128 experts, 1 million context, about 22 trillion tokens. Cutoff August 2024. [cite:2]</p><h3>L4 · Why is sampler temperature not attention temperature?</h3><p>OpenAI’s chat reference divides logits by temperature before the vocabulary softmax, range 0 to 2. The blog’s attention-temperature scaling is inside iRoPE. Different objects. [cite:4] [cite:3]</p><h3>L4 · What must you not copy from the paper onto gpt-6-astra?</h3><p>Layer count, head count, and d_model. The models page fetched 2026-10-14 publishes context and max output, not those widths. [cite:6]</p><h3>L5 · If you redesigned the debug UI, what would you change, and what stops you?</h3><p>I would show the formula and the mask, and I would refuse a heatmap labeled as the reason for a refund. What stops a looser UI is the absence of that product’s own evaluation. Check it before you call a map the reason; faithfulness varies by model and by task. Check the serving stack for cache bytes; the size varies with length, layers, precision, and batch. [cite:1]</p><h3>Leaf · Where does a missing policy PDF get mixed in?</h3><p>It does not. Attention mixes tokens that are already in the window. Pack the PDF or call a tool. The head will not fetch it. [cite:8]</p><h3>Leaf · Name the license if you serve Llama 4 weights.</h3><p>The Llama 4 Community License Agreement, effective 5 April 2025. Not MIT. The acceptable-use policy is a separate document the card points at. [cite:9]</p><h3>09Lab</h3><p>No API key. Paper, or the sampling lab’s spirit: numbers only.</p><ol><li>Prerequisite: T1-R01. You can say what a logit is.</li><li>Compute the toy: q=[1,0], keys [1,0] and [0,1], d_k=2. Write scaled scores and softmax weights to two decimals.</li><li>Zero the future key and recompute. The weight on that key is 0.</li><li>Write one sentence that separates sampler temperature from the blog’s attention-temperature scaling.</li><li>From the Llama 4 card, state Scout’s active parameters, expert count, and context-length field without looking.</li><li>Stop. Do not invent a head count for an OpenAI model id. Do not paste 28.4 BLEU into a contact-center slide.</li></ol><h3>10Quiz</h3><p>Recall</p><h3>Q1. Scaled dot-product attention is:</h3><h3>Reveal</h3><p>softmax of QK transpose over the square root of d_k, times V. [cite:1]</p><p>Apply</p><h3>Q2. In the toy, d_k is 2 and the raw dots are 1 and 0. What do you divide by?</h3><h3>Reveal</h3><p>The square root of 2, before softmax. Skipping the scale is a different function. [cite:1]</p><p>Apply</p><h3>Q3. A future key under the causal mask has weight:</h3><h3>Reveal</h3><p>Zero, because its score was set so softmax assigns it no mass. The paper’s decoder is causal. [cite:1]</p><p>Recall</p><h3>Q4. The 2017 base model’s head count is:</h3><h3>Reveal</h3><p>8, with d_model 512. Historical. Not a 2026 product constant. [cite:1]</p><p>Apply</p><h3>Q5. A teammate sets gpt-6-astra’s heads to 8 because “transformers have 8.”</h3><h3>Reveal</h3><p>The models page fetched 2026-10-14 does not publish that width. Refuse the copy. [cite:6]</p><p>Recall</p><h3>Q6. Llama 4 Scout, on the model card:</h3><h3>Reveal</h3><p>17B active, 109B total, 16 experts, context length 10M, knowledge cutoff August 2024. [cite:2]</p><p>Apply</p><h3>Q7. Someone says Scout was only trained at 10M context.</h3><h3>Reveal</h3><p>The card’s context field is 10M. The blog says Scout was pre-trained and post-trained with a 256K context, which empowers length generalization, and it names a 10 million token supported context. Keep both. [cite:3]</p><p>Recall</p><h3>Q8. iRoPE, as the blog names it, includes:</h3><h3>Reveal</h3><p>RoPE on most layers, interleaved layers without positional embeddings, and inference-time temperature scaling of attention. [cite:3]</p><p>Apply</p><h3>Q9. Raising API temperature to 1.4 changes iRoPE’s attention temperature.</h3><h3>Reveal</h3><p>No. Those are different scales. Chat-completions temperature divides logits and is documented from 0 to 2. [cite:4]</p><p>Apply</p><h3>Q10. The brightest attention weight is why the bot promised a credit.</h3><h3>Reveal</h3><p>The paper defines a mix, not a faithful explanation. Grade the promise against the pack. Product claims of faithfulness stay unverified here. [cite:1]</p><p>Recall</p><h3>Q11. The feed-forward sublayer in the paper mixes:</h3><h3>Reveal</h3><p>Features at one position. Attention mixes positions. Retrieval is neither of those. [cite:1]</p><p>Apply</p><h3>Q12. You will serve Llama 4 weights. The license to open is:</h3><h3>Reveal</h3><p>The Llama 4 Community License, effective 5 April 2025. It is not the MIT line from an orchestration framework. [cite:9]</p><h3>11Audio</h3><p>Silence.
